description:
FILED s536 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-08) while keying the round board's YAML-Tiny row.

REPRODUCER (scratchpad yt.pl; latin1.txt = the bytes `caf\xe9: x\n`):
    open my $fh, "<:utf8", $file or die; my $s = do { local $/; local $SIG{__WARN__} = sub {}; <$fh> };
    print "1 len=", length($s), " is_utf8=", (utf8::is_utf8($s) ? 1 : 0), " valid=", (utf8::valid($s) ? 1 : 0), "\n";
  perl 5.40.3: `1 len=6 is_utf8=1 valid=0`.   PCL (MAIN-READY-76): `1 len= is_utf8=0 valid=1` -- the slurp is UNDEF: the whole read is lost.

WHY IT MATTERS: the :utf8 layer (unlike :encoding(UTF-8)) does not validate -- perl reads the octets and marks them utf8; a malformed sequence is a malformed string, and modules detect it with utf8::valid / utf8::decode / Encode (YAML::Tiny `read_string` dies "invalid UTF-8 string").  PCL loses the data.  The representation half (a string can not be "utf8-flagged but malformed" in PCL) is #1389's family (the utf8 flag); the LOSS of the read is not -- at minimum the read must return the text (each bad byte as its own character, as :encoding does with a substitution, or perl's lax octets) and say what it did.

ROWS: cpan-tests/modules/YAML-Tiny-1.74 t/11_read_string.t row 4 "invalid UTF-8" (reached since MAIN-READY-66/-67, when the file stopped dying at its *PLAN*; blessed s536 by edit with this key).
WHERE TO START: the input layer's UTF-8 decoder (`:utf8` read path in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, the readline / slurp of a decoding handle) -- find what it does on an invalid sequence (signal caught and the read abandoned?).  Rule 12: a decode failure that silently drops the read is the worst case.
subject: SILENT WRONG: reading INVALID UTF-8 (Latin-1 bytes) through a `:utf8` layer answers UNDEF -- perl's lax :utf8 layer returns the bytes as a utf8-flagged string that utf8::valid rejects (YAML-Tiny t/11_read_string.t row 4 "invalid UTF-8")
